title: Inference economics: Optimize playbook and KV-prefetch cost model with AetherWorks
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked AetherWorks through Optimize recommendations focusing on batching, prefix/KV caching and a simple cost model. Discussed production constraints (latency SLOs, PII retention), choice between hosted vs dedicated, and a pilot roadmap. Action items include security docs, a 2-week sandbox, and an initial cost spreadsheet tailored to their session profile.
topics: Batching strategies: concurrency vs continuous batching
Prefix/KV cache: hit rates, sessionization, eviction policies
Cost model: tokens, GPU time, reserved capacity impact
transcript: [00:00] Samir: Good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood, AE for this region. Claire, would you like to intro?

[00:08] Claire: Hi, yes thanks. Claire Nguyen, solutions engineer. We'll walk through the Optimize playbook — batching, prefix or KV cache options, and a small cost model we made looking at AetherWorks' demo profile you sent. Feel free to interrupt.

[00:22] Mariela: Thanks, quick note — we're on a tight timeline, want a pilot in two weeks if feasible. Latency SLO is 150ms p95 for short responses, but some flows can be 600 tokens. Also, we have PII concerns so data residency/VPC is important.
[00:37] Samir: Great, timeline noted. Claire, maybe start with the high level tradeoffs?

[00:41] Claire: Sure. Two levers we normally tune: batching — which reduces per-token compute by packing requests, and prefix/KV caching — which saves repeated prefix decode work for sessionized assistants. With your traffic profile — session length median ~ 40 tokens, 10 requests per session — we estimate big wins from KV cache if hit rates exceed about 30%.
[01:05] Devon: Sorry can you say that again — hit rate threshold?

[01:07] Claire: Yeah so with our cost model, if your effective cache hit rate is above ~30% for prefixes we see net cost savings even after added memory overhead + slightly higher tail latency from cache lookups. Below that, batching/concurrency tuning usually gives better ROI.
[01:22] Rohan: What's the mechanism for session affinity? We run across multiple pods behind a load balancer, don't want KV misses because of sharding.

[01:28] Claire: Good question. For private/dedicated deployments we recommend session affinity at the routing layer — sticky session tokens routed to the node with cached KV. For hosted, Redwood routes by policy and will warm small CS cache replicas; we also support a centralized KV layer that can be attached to Dedicated clusters to avoid affinity but with slightly higher lookup latency.
[01:47] Mariela: And what about fallback? If cache misses spike, do we auto-scale?
[01:50] Samir: Yes, we have two policies: automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant or surge capacity from dedicated pools. Claire will show the console policy demo shortly.

[01:58] Claire: Jumping to the console — (screen-share noise) — on the Optimize tab you'll see a recommended profile. For AetherWorks I uploaded your sample trace. See here: baseline cost per 1M tokens with no cache: about $980 (hosted baseline). With moderate batching (batch window 20ms, concurrency 12) we drop to ~$650. Adding a 40% KV hit rate drops costs to ~$420. These are ballpark, your real numbers depend on tokenization dynamics and sequence lengths.
[02:26] Devon: That $980 number is per 1M generated tokens? What about input tokens? We do a lot of long contexts from knowledge bases.
[02:32] Claire: Good catch — yes the model charge includes both input and output tokens; I used your distribution where input:output is about 1.2x. We can split that in the spreadsheet.
[02:42] Mariela: How accurate is the model for large bursts? We have hourly spikes during product launches and can't tolerate big latency increases.

[02:47] Claire: For spikes we advise two things: 1) Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable baseline throughput; 2) a burst policy that allows short-lived excess capacity in hosted with pre-warmed LRU workers. In our sim, keeping a small reserved pool that covers your 75th percentile removes most latency spikes and the incremental cost is modest compared to full overprovisioning.
[03:05] Rohan: Security — we need SOC2, SSO via SAML, and KMS integration for keys. Also audit logs retained 13 months. Does Redwood support all those in Private?

[03:12] Samir: Yes — Private supports SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM integrations, and customizable audit log retention. For hosted we have SOC2 and 90-day logs by default; enterprise options extend retention. We'll send a redlined security pack after the call.
[03:25] Priya: Procurement question — if we go Dedicated reserved, what's minimum term?
[03:29] Samir: Typical committed capacity contracts are 3 or 12 months. For pilots we do a 6-week reserved eval with prorated billing in many cases. We'll note that as an option.

[03:36] Claire: Back to caching — two caching patterns: prefix cache (store decoder kv-cache for common prompts) and structured KV for retrieval-augmented flows. Prefix cache tends to work great for assistant-like session histories; structured KV is better for repeated retrieval of doc embeddings. For your use case (recurrent assistant prompts), prefix/KV is the primary lever.
[03:57] Devon: Do we need model changes or quantization? We're currently using an FP16 variant and want to keep quality identical.

[04:02] Claire: Prefetch and cache don't require model changes; they just store model state. Quantization is a separate axis — we can recommend low-precision variants and show quality diffs. For your SLO of 150ms p95, FP16 on dedicated T4-like devices with batching tuned is usually safe, but if you need extreme latency you'd consider lower sequence models or routing to smaller context variants.
[04:22] Mariela: Can you show an example of the cost spreadsheet?

[04:25] Claire: Sure — (shares spreadsheet) Column A: traffic mix; Column B: avg tokens per request; Column C: cache hit rate scenarios 0/20/40/60; Column D: host GPU seconds; Column E: estimated $/1M tokens. For example sample row: avg tokens 48, concurrency 10, no cache: $1,020; 40% cache: $460. I'll email the sheet.
[04:47] Rohan: We're worried about cache eviction during upgrades — do you persist kv across version rollouts?

[04:52] Claire: We have migration helpers — two strategies: warm new model nodes before cutover, or use a shared KV store that is model-version aware. Both are supported; tradeoffs are complexity vs latency. We'll outline the recommended approach in the runbook we send.
[05:05] Devon: What about observability? We need token-level cost attribution per route and tracing into prefetch hits/misses.

[05:11] Samir: Redwood Console provides token-level breakdowns by route and model. Optimize adds cache hit/miss dashboards and a throughput simulator — Claire will demo the simulator next to show heat maps of session affinity.

[05:22] Claire: (simulator demo) Here you can toggle session stickiness and watch simulated p95 latency vs cost. Notice as we increase session affinity from 0% to 80%, cache hit rate climbs sharply and cost drops non-linearly. But tail latency can rise slightly if affinity causes hot nodes — that's why a small reserved pool helps.
[05:42] Mariela: Is there any additional engineering work on our side to enable prefix cache?

[05:47] Claire: Minimal — you need to pass a session id and allow the same prompt keying. If using our SDK, it's a one-line flag. For on-prem we will coordinate with your infra team to ensure the routing policy is installed.
[05:58] Devon: Can Redwood run a 48-hour benchmark against our traffic?

06:01] Samir: Yes, we offer a sandbox benchmark. For dedicated pilots we can spin a reserved test cluster. We'll need a scrubbed traffic trace — you can send a 24–48 hour trace with PII redacted and we'll run the sim and return detailed per-route cost projections.
[06:15] Priya: On procurement timing, if the pilot goes well, what's typical lead time to turn on dedicated?

[06:19] Samir: For a standard configuration it's 2–4 weeks after contract signature to provision dedicated pools in a given region, faster if using existing capacity. For private on-prem it's collection-dependent and usually longer.

[06:28] Claire: Quick demo of an Optimize rule: here we set a policy to route requests under 50 tokens to a low-latency variant, longer contexts to a high-throughput variant, and enable KV prefetch for sticky sessions. You can also set a cost-savings target and the optimizer will auto-propose batching windows and concurrency levels.
[06:48] Devon: Does the optimizer ever sacrifice quality for cost? How deterministic is it?

06:51] Claire: It doesn't change model weights. It recommends smaller variants or quantized builds which may impact outputs; we attach eval diffs to each suggestion. Customers choose thresholds for acceptable ROUGE/EM or human-rated deltas.
[07:03] Mariela: Let's talk numbers — if we commit to a 6-month dedicated pool that covers 50% baseline traffic, what's the expected unit cost reduction?

[07:09] Samir: Ballpark: dedicated reserved typically reduces per-token infra cost by ~30–45% versus hosted at scale because of amortized GPU utilization. Combined with 40% cache hits you'd see up to ~65% reduction vs baseline hosted no-cache scenario in our model. We'll provide a detailed spreadsheet with assumptions.
[07:28] Rohan: Are there any single points of failure with centralized cache?

07:31] Claire: Centralized stores are architected with regional replicas and cross-zone redundancy. For on-prem private installs we recommend a small cluster with leader election to avoid SPOF. We'll include HA topology in the runbook.
[07:45] Priya: On invoices, can you show a sample of how reserved + usage billing looks?
[07:49] Samir: Yes we'll send a sample invoice template showing committed capacity line items, overage charges, and per-route usage columns.
[07:58] Mariela: Ok if we proceed with a pilot, we'd need: 1) security pack, 2) cost spreadsheet with our 30-day traffic, 3) a 2-week sandbox to run the benchmark. Can you confirm?
[08:08] Samir: Confirmed. Claire, any final notes?

[08:11] Claire: Just a quick note: one practical trick — prefix canonicalization. If you normalize prompts to a consistent key (strip timestamps/user IDs/etc.) hit rates jump a lot. Many teams forget that and shower cache misses. We'll include examples in the runbook.
[08:26] Devon: Nice, that sounds useful.
[08:29] Mariela: Who will be our Redwood POC during the pilot?
[08:31] Samir: I'll be AE contact, Claire will be your technical lead. We'll also loop in Solutions Ops for the provisioning. I'll send calendar invites for a kickoff next Tuesday.
[08:40] Priya: Can we get estimated cost per month for a conservative and aggressive scenario?

[08:43] Claire: Yes conservative (20% cache, minimal reserved pool): ~$9k/mo; aggressive (50% cache, reserved baseline sized to 75th percentile): ~$4.2k/mo. These are quick-n-look numbers; spreadsheet will have detailed assumptions.
[08:58] Rohan: About the simulator — can we run it against our historical traces?
09:01] Claire: Absolutely, that's how we generate the per-route recommendations. Send an anonymized trace and we'll ingest it into the sandbox.
[09:08] Mariela: Any legal hurdles with us sending traces? We need a DPA in place.
[09:12] Samir: We'll send a DPA template; for the sandbox we accept scrubbed/anonymized data. We'll coordinate with your legal team.
[09:21] Claire: Quick Q/A: Priya asked earlier about log retention beyond 90 days in hosted — that is available as an enterprise add-on and we can include it in the pilot contract.
[09:29] Priya: Great.
[09:32] Samir: Alright let's recap and next steps, I want to make sure timelines are clear.

[09:36] Samir: 1) We'll email security pack and DPA — Samir to own, by 2027-02-11. 2) A two-week sandbox benchmark — Claire to schedule and run; we need an anonymized 48-hour trace by 2027-02-12. 3) Cost spreadsheet tailored to your profile — Claire will email same day as the benchmark results. 4) Pilot kickoff: propose next Tuesday 2027-02-16 — Samir to send invite. Exceptions?
[10:04] Mariela: Dates work, we'll try to get the trace to you by the 12th but might need 1 extra day.
[10:10] Devon: One more thing — can you include a short checklist of minimal SDK changes? We're a small infra team.
[10:15] Claire: Yes, we'll include a 1-page SDK checklist and a sample config snippet.
[10:20] Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and invites. End of call.
[10:22] (call ends)
